recentKeyChanges.title: Q2 paid miles actually fell 36% QoQ — hot context understated the decline
recentKeyChanges.description: Multiple credible sources including TechCrunch (July 23) and Tesla's own Q2 cumulative-miles chart confirm that Tesla Robotaxi paid miles fell approximately 36% quarter-over-quarter: Q1 2026 was roughly 1.1 million paid miles, Q2 2026 was roughly 700,000 — not 'flat' at ~900k as framed in Q2 materials. The prior week's hot context accepted Tesla's cumulative 2.4M figure and derived ~900k Q2 by differencing; multiple outlets now show Tesla's own per-quarter disclosure puts Q1 higher (~1.1M) and Q2 lower (~700k). Tesla's explanation is that the company deliberately redirected Model Y robotaxi miles toward Cybercab-specific data collection. Analysts and investors have not accepted that framing — TSLA fell ~14.5% post-earnings in part on this data. The active unsupervised fleet remains approximately 21 vehicles after ~14 months of paid commercial service. Phoenix and Las Vegas were listed in the Q2 letter as 'preparations underway' — no confirmed launch in this period.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Tesla's own figures, now properly read quarter-to-quarter, show a 36% decline in paid miles — not growth and not flat. The safety/data-collection narrative is a rationalization, not a plan. Fleet has not grown in 14 months.

recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla quietly removes 'volume production in 2026' language for Cybercab from Q2 shareholder letter
recentKeyChanges.description: In its Q2 2026 shareholder letter (July 22, widely reported July 23), Tesla removed explicit 'volume production in 2026' commitments for the Cybercab, Tesla Semi, and Megapack 3 — language that was present as recently as the Q1 2026 letter. TechCrunch's analysis of the letter diff confirmed the deletion. Tesla's new language describes Cybercab as being in 'start of production' with volume dependent on scaling 4680 battery cell output. The company said it is working to increase 4680 production to support Cybercab and Semi at scale. No replacement timeline was provided. This is the second time Tesla has silently walked back a Cybercab production milestone: the original June 2025 'before end of year' public launch slipped, and now 2026 volume production has been dropped without acknowledgment. The Cybercab at this date has 245 units staged at Giga Texas, zero in paid fleet service, and is in an on-campus employee ride phase plus on-road engineering test phase in Austin.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Silent removal of volume production timeline is a material negative. Production is real but 'volume' in 2026 is now off the table per Tesla's own letter. No new timeline given.

recentKeyChanges.title: Cybercabs appear in Charlotte, NC — 14 units with Texas plates, AI Safety Operator job posted
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 25-27, 2026, observer reports and Axios Charlotte confirmed 14 Tesla Cybercabs and 14 Model Y vehicles bearing Texas plates in a Charlotte-area parking lot — the first confirmed out-of-state Cybercab deployment destination from the Giga Texas staging inventory. Tesla simultaneously posted an AI Safety Operator job for Charlotte to 'oversee daily operations of ride-hailing services' and collect data by driving in a 'designated area' for 6-8 hours per day. This mirrors the exact playbook Tesla ran before every prior robotaxi market launch: vehicle pre-positioning followed by safety-operator-supervised data-collection rides before unsupervised public service. Charlotte is not a launched market — it is the earliest pre-launch data-collection phase. Waymo has also been testing in Charlotte for months, setting up a potential direct competitive confrontation. The key read: Charlotte's appearance is the first evidence that Cybercabs are physically leaving Giga Texas for operational staging, which is required before any paid service — but it is phase zero of a multi-phase process that took Austin roughly 12 months from vehicle arrival to unsupervised paid rides.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Cybercabs physically leaving Texas for a new city is a real operational step. But the pattern from every prior market shows 6-12 months between vehicle arrival and paid unsupervised service. Charlotte is in data-collection phase zero.
